newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Africa Israel sabbath move riles.
newsitem.headline: Africa Israel sabbath move riles.

text.p: Africa Israel Investments Ltd's decision this week that a shopping mall planned for the secular heart of Tel Aviv will be shut on the Jewish sabbath has put the development company in the eye of a storm.

The decision, taken at a board meeting on March 3, comes three months after Lev Leviev, an ultra-Orthodox Jew, acquired a controlling stake in Africa Israel. Jewish ritual law bans work on the sabbath.
The company's move has fuelled the ever-burning debate in Israel between those who observe Jewish ritual laws covering everything from food to work -- and the majority of Israelis who do not.
The Israeli franchiser of the fast food giant McDonald's, set to occupy a store in the mall slated to open in July, is enraged by the move.
"It's ridiculous in the main secular area of Israel they are trying to close movie theatres and restaurants. No one expected it," McDonald's Israel managing director Omri Padan told Reuters.
One leading Israeli business writer said the move smacked of Iranian-style religious compulsion.

"The ultra-Orthodox are trying to impose an Iranian-style regime on the secular majority," Nehamia Strasler, a business editor at Israel's Haaretz daily, wrote in an opinion piece published in the Jerusalem Post this week.
The article was headlined: "The Ayatollah of Ramat Aviv". The mall is to be in the suburb of Ramat Aviv.
"If the mall remains closed on Saturdays as planned, it will cut into Africa Israel profits," Stradler added.
Israel's Bank Leumi, which has a 25 percent stake in Africa Israel, did not want to relate to any possible losses.
"The bank does not commment on companies in which it holds shares. The directors (at Africa Israel) from the bank act for the good of the company," a bank spokeswoman said.
Africa Israel managing director Avigdor Kaplan, appointed on January 29 the same day Leviev was named company chairman, shrugged off the criticism.
"Let's put it in proportion. Most malls are closed on the sabbath," Kaplan said, adding that Africa Israel was guided by professional considerations at all times.
Kaplan dismissed the local media storm at the board's unanimous decision. "Articles like that have a political nature and I don't want to enter into a political, emotional problem."

Padan said McDonald's had a contract that stipulated the mall franchise would not have to abide by Jewish kosher dietary laws and could open on the sabbath if movie theatres were to be open as well, a matter that had yet to be settled when Africa Israel's board took its decision.

Kaplan said the board pledged to abide by signed agreements when it took the decision. He said Africa Israel had yet to finalise a contract with McDonald's so closing the mall on the sabbath violated nothing between the firms.

Leviev, who was a leading figure in the Israeli diamond industry, paid $141 million for a stake of Africa Israel from Leumi and another $49 million for shares controlled by Israeli businessmen Mordechai Zisser and Eitan Wertheimer.
The combined stakes were equal to 46.58 percent of equity in Africa and 54.2 percent of voting rights.
Leumi, which previously controlled Africa Israel, was forced to reduce its stake to 25 percent under bank reform laws and will have to reduce it to 20 percent by 1999.
